risks.risk: Dependence on, and alleged obstruction by, the West Bengal State Excise administration
risks.note: Both the distillery and the IML business are described as disrupted by what management calls illegal methods and illegal interference by State Excise authorities - customers reluctant to lift material, retailers threatened with dire consequences and forced not to lift the IFB branded product. Representations to the Excise Commissioner have been pending since 2020 and further representation was made to the then Chief Minister. This is a structural regulatory-relationship risk that management says has already caused intermittent stoppage of production.

risks.risk: ENA / ODS overcapacity in West Bengal compressing distillery margins
risks.note: Several newly commissioned ethanol distilleries with dual ENA production facilities have intensified competition in the State. Distillery margins were hit by stiff price cuts in ENA and Ordinary Denatured Spirit, and the outlook section states the current financial year will be a year of challenges for the Alcohol business with margin likely impacted by excess supply, higher non-edible grain prices and lower ENA prices.

risks.risk: By-product price erosion (DDGS and carbon dioxide)
risks.note: Prices of Distiller's Dried Grains with Soluble and carbon di-oxide have decreased because of excess supply from the new ethanol plants, removing a margin cushion that the distillery model relies on.

risks.risk: Excise duty escalation shrinking the IML consumer base
risks.note: The IML industry in Bengal grew only about 3% over the last 2 years because of frequent price increases by the Excise Department, with a further duty increase effective 1 December 2025. Management says the abnormal price increase has forced lower-income consumers to shift toward smaller pack sizes - a mix and volume risk driven entirely by a third party.

risks.risk: Ethanol revenue is gated on external tender timing
risks.note: The newly commissioned 25 KLPD ethanol plant was completed during the year but sales will only start in FY 26-27 and only once new tenders are floated by the Oil and Marketing Companies, so an installed asset earns nothing until an external process runs.

risks.risk: Raw shrimp seasonality with single-location processing
risks.note: Raw shrimp is unavailable in West Bengal for almost 6-7 months in a year and the processing unit is situated in West Bengal only, which management explicitly calls out as making the marine business more challenging - a combined input-availability and geographic-concentration risk.

risks.risk: US tariffs and geopolitical disruption to the shrimp export trade
risks.note: Shrimp exports from India to the USA, the largest destination for Indian exporters, faced severe challenge from US tariffs; the Company's own dependence on the USA is limited and its marine export still rose from ` 213 Crs. to ` 273 Crs. Geopolitical uncertainties have separately raised pricing volatility, ocean freight and delivery delays from non-availability of shipping lines.

risks.risk: Aqua feed input costs cannot be passed on under Andhra Pradesh price control
risks.note: The newly acquired aqua feed business is expected to face severe challenge because significantly higher input prices could not be passed on to consumers, the Andhra Pradesh Government having disallowed shrimp feed price increases - a state-administered price cap sitting directly on the segment the Company has just bought into.

The Board has adopted a risk management policy to identify and evaluate business risks and threats and constituted a Risk Management Committee at its meeting dated 9 August 2021 under Regulation 21 of the SEBI LODR, with structures stated to be in place to proactively monitor businesses with unique or relatively high-risk profiles. The AR does not enumerate a risk register in this routed text.

hero.oneLiner: IFB Agro Industries is a West Bengal-based alcohol and marine products company - distilling ENA, ODS and ethanol and selling IFB-branded Indian Made Liquor, processing and exporting shrimp - which in FY2025-26 added an aquaculture feed business acquired from Cargill India.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: IFB Agro Industries is a West Bengal-based alcohol and marine products company - distilling ENA, ODS and ethanol and selling IFB-branded Indian Made Liquor, processing and exporting shrimp - which in FY2025-26 added an aquaculture feed business acquired from Cargill India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company operates in two reported segments: (1) Spirit, Spirituous Beverages and allied products and (2) Marine Products. The distillery makes Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), Ordinary Denatured Spirit (ODS) and, from a newly commissioned 25 KLPD plant, ethanol, with Distiller's Dried Grains with Soluble (DDGS) and carbon dioxide as by-products, while the IML business sells IFB-branded Indian Made Liquor in West Bengal. The marine business processes shrimp in West Bengal for export (USA, Russia, Europe, Japan) and sells domestically to retail and HORECA, and from 1 August 2025 the Company also manufactures commercial compound shrimp feed and freshwater fish feed at Vijayawada and Rajahmundry after acquiring that business from Cargill India Private Limited.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- IFB Agro Holdings Pte. Ltd. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary in Singapore, 100% held at both 31 March 2026 and 31 March 2025; acquired 20 June 2023; acts as the holding company for the Vietnam step-down subsidiary
- IFB Vietnam Company Ltd — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary in Vietnam, held through IFB Agro Holdings Pte. Ltd; the related-party note shows no direct shareholding percentage for it in either year
- IFB Agro Marine (FZE) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary in the Sharjah Airport International Free Zone, UAE, incorporated 20 April 2017 and shown as acquired 20-April-2017 in Form AOC-1; 100% held at 31 March 2025 and nil at 31 March 2026. The Board approved closure on 11 November 2024 and the entity was closed with effect from 25 September 2025
- IFB Industries Limited — related party: The Corporate Governance directorship table records Mr. Bikramjit Nag - Chairman and Promoter of IFB Agro - as Chairman of IFB Industries Limited, his only other listed-entity directorship. This bundle's RPT 'Other related parties' list is cut off mid-name, so the AR's own related-party classification of this entity is not visible here
- Associates and joint ventures — associate: Form AOC-1 Part B states that there are no associates and joint ventures as at 31 March 2026, so Part B has not been furnished - an explicit nil, not a gap

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Spirit, Spirituous Beverages and allied products:** Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), Ordinary Denatured Spirit (ODS), Ethanol, Indian Made Liquor (IML) - IFB branded product, Distiller's Dried Grains with Soluble (DDGS) (by-product), Carbon di-oxide (CO2) (by-product)
- **Marine Products:** Processed shrimp for export, Value added shrimp products (Vietnam project), Domestic branded retail and HORECA seafood
- **Marine Feed Division:** Commercial compound shrimp feed, Freshwater fish feed

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- USA (largest shrimp export destination for India; Company's dependence described as limited)
- Russia
- Europe
- Japan
- West Bengal - distillery (ENA/ODS) and IML retail trade
- Andhra Pradesh - shrimp feed, where the State Government controls feed prices
- Indian domestic seafood retail and HORECA, including Q-commerce and E-commerce
- Oil Marketing Companies - ethanol, via tenders expected in FY 26-27

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Distillery margins are likely to be impacted in the current financial year by excess ENA capacity set up in West Bengal, increased demand for non-edible grain from ethanol plants pushing input prices up, and lower ENA prices including by-products
- By-product realisations (DDGS and carbon dioxide) have fallen because of excess supply from newly commissioned ethanol plants
- Rapid expansion of the ethanol industry in West Bengal, with several newly commissioned distilleries carrying dual ENA production facilities, has intensified competition in the State
- Ethanol revenue is gated on new tenders being floated by the Oil and Marketing Companies in FY 26-27
- IML volumes in Bengal are constrained by repeated excise duty increases (a further increase effective 1 December 2025) that have pushed lower-income consumers toward smaller pack sizes; the IML industry in Bengal grew only about 3% over the last 2 years
- Distillery and IML offtake has been disrupted by what management describes as illegal interference by State Excise authorities, with representations pending with the Excise Commissioner since 2020; management hopes for a more conducive business environment under the new State Government
- Aqua feed margins are under pressure because significantly higher input prices could not be passed on, as the Andhra Pradesh Government has not allowed shrimp feed prices to be increased
- US tariffs on Indian shrimp are a headwind for the export industry, though the Company's own dependence on the USA market is limited - its marine export rose from ` 213 Crs. to ` 273 Crs.
- Raw shrimp is unavailable in West Bengal for roughly 6-7 months a year and the processing unit is located only in West Bengal, constraining marine operations
- Geopolitical uncertainty is raising export pricing volatility, ocean freight and delivery delays from non-availability of shipping lines
- Domestic marine food demand is a growth driver - the domestic business grew 23% on both retail and HORECA, with branded retail up 90%, largely through Q-commerce and E-commerce
- Management expects the integration of the newly acquired Aqua Feed business to strengthen market presence across states and improve margins in FY 2026-27, and remains cautiously optimistic overall

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strategic entry into the aquaculture feed segment via acquisition of Cargill India Private Limited's commercial compound shrimp feed and freshwater fish feed business, effective 1 August 2025, including the Vijayawada and Rajahmundry manufacturing facilities, distribution network, feed formulations, contracts, licences and employees - framed as backward integration into the shrimp and fish farming value chain
- Grow the acquired aqua feed business during 2026-27 and lift margins and returns on capital employed through better procurement of key raw materials (non-edible rice, shrimps) and tight control over overheads
- Optimise capacity utilisation of the acquired Andhra facilities before expanding feed manufacturing capacity, which is planned for the next 1-2 years
- Make the capex-light value-added seafood project in Vietnam (machinery installed in a third party plant, run through IFB Vietnam Company Ltd) successful and take it to break even, shifting the product profile from traditional frozen to value-added shrimp
- Further expansion in the Marine business, with resource allocation focused on it
- Evaluate 2-3 new growth projects relating to Glycerine and Bio Gas, closing at least one by Q3 of FY 2026-27
- Commissioned a 25 KLPD ethanol plant at the distillery to enter ethanol supply, with sales to begin in FY 26-27 on OMC tenders
- Grow the branded domestic marine food business through product innovation and marketing, leveraging Q-commerce and E-commerce to take the brand Pan-India
- Keep the Balasore feed manufacturing project in abeyance in view of the recent acquisition
- Pursue continuing efficiency gains through process and technological improvements, reduction of wastages and optimal use of human resources across all divisions
- Retain balance-sheet flexibility: debt was strategically availed to fund the acquisition while keeping sufficient cash reserve for future expansion and/or potential acquisitions, leaving the Company net-debt zero as on 31 March 2026
- Conserve resources for further expansion and working capital by not recommending a dividend for the year
- The Board adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy at its meeting held on August 9, 2021 pursuant to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, and the policy is available at www.ifbagro.in. This bundle records only the fact of the policy's adoption and its web availability - the policy's own contents, any payout parameters and the dividend decision for the year are not present in the routed text, so no payout or reinvestment philosophy can be stated from it. On CSR, the Board has constituted a CSR Committee comprising Independent Directors and an Executive Director, with projects directed at eradicating hunger, malnutrition and sanitation, promoting education, promoting healthcare and safe drinking water, and rural development and livelihood enhancement; the Company spent ` 64.64 lakhs on CSR against a stipulated amount of Rs. 62.05 lakhs.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The year's principal expansion was inorganic: with effect from 1 August 2025 the Company acquired the shrimp feed and freshwater fish feed business of Cargill India Private Limited - which had an annual turnover of ` 353 Crs. as on 31 March 2025 - for ` 110 Crs. plus working capital, taking over established manufacturing facilities at Vijayawada and Rajahmundry along with the distribution network, product portfolio, feed formulations, contracts, licences, employees and associated business assets. On the organic side, a newly set up 25 KLPD Ethanol plant at the distillery was successfully commissioned during the year, though ethanol sales will only begin in FY 26-27 once the Oil and Marketing Companies float new tenders. The value-added seafood project in Vietnam is deliberately capex-light - key machineries installed in a third party plant, operated through step-down subsidiary IFB Vietnam Company Ltd - and moved during the year from development and product validation to initial commercial operations, with the first shipment in April 2026; management's focus for the current year is to grow it to break even. In view of the aqua-feed acquisition the feed manufacturing project at Balasore has been kept in abeyance. Looking forward, the Chairman states the Company is actively evaluating 2-3 projects relating to Glycerine and Bio Gas and will close at least one by Q3 of the current financial year, and plans to expand feed manufacturing capacity in the next 1-2 years once the capacities at the existing Andhra plants are fully utilised; near-term focus is on optimising utilisation of the acquired facilities. The acquisition was funded by debt strategically availed while keeping cash reserve for future expansion and/or potential acquisitions, and no dividend was recommended so as to conserve resources for further expansion and working capital.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Limited dependence on the USA market: marine exports rose from ` 213 Crs. to ` 273 Crs. even as US tariffs hit Indian shrimp exports
- Acquired an established aqua-feed platform - manufacturing facilities at Vijayawada and Rajahmundry with a well-entrenched distribution network, product portfolio, feed formulations and associated business assets
- Identifiable IML brand franchise in West Bengal - the AR describes retailers being pressured 'not to lift the IFB branded product'
- Distillery with by-product streams (DDGS, CO2) alongside ENA/ODS and a newly commissioned 25 KLPD ethanol line
- Long Term issuer rating maintained at 'IND A+' by India Ratings and Research during the year
- Balance-sheet capacity for expansion: the Chairman states debt of ` 70.00 crore against a cash balance of ` 183 crore and describes the Company as Net Debt zero as on 31 March 2026
- Fast-growing branded domestic seafood business - domestic marine food business grew 23% and branded retail grew 90% over last year, largely through Q-commerce and E-commerce

- US tariffs and geopolitical disruption to the shrimp export trade — Shrimp exports from India to the USA, the largest destination for Indian exporters, faced severe challenge from US tariffs; the Company's own dependence on the USA is limited and its marine export still rose from ` 213 Crs. to ` 273 Crs. Geopolitical uncertainties have separately raised pricing volatility, ocean freight and delivery delays from non-availability of shipping lines.
- Aqua feed input costs cannot be passed on under Andhra Pradesh price control — The newly acquired aqua feed business is expected to face severe challenge because significantly higher input prices could not be passed on to consumers, the Andhra Pradesh Government having disallowed shrimp feed price increases - a state-administered price cap sitting directly on the segment the Company has just bought into.
- Enterprise risk governance framework — The Board has adopted a risk management policy to identify and evaluate business risks and threats and constituted a Risk Management Committee at its meeting dated 9 August 2021 under Regulation 21 of the SEBI LODR, with structures stated to be in place to proactively monitor businesses with unique or relatively high-risk profiles. The AR does not enumerate a risk register in this routed text.
